source: The Man Who Poisoned the World Twice, v3 spec shots k01-k18

beats.direction: Quiet intrigue, a storyteller setting a scene.
beats.text: October, 1924. A room full of reporters in New York.
A man in a neat bow tie steps up to a table.
He pours a clear liquid over his hands.
Then he holds the bottle under his nose, and breathes it in. [pause] For a <stress>full minute</stress>.
He smiles. [pause] The reporters write it all down.

beats.direction: Darker and slower, the smile is gone.
beats.text: Days earlier, workers making that same liquid had started to die.
And you are probably still carrying a piece of it. [pause] Right now.
So how did one cheap additive end up inside almost every human on Earth?
And why did it take a <stress>hundred years</stress> to get it out?
To understand it, we have to go back. Dayton, Ohio. 1921.
America has fallen in love with the car. [pause] But the car has a problem.
Push the engine harder, and it starts to <stress>knock</stress>.
Knocking wastes power, and it can tear the engine apart.
General Motors wants it fixed. Its research chief, Charles Kettering, wants it fixed <stress>fast</stress>.
So he hands the job to a young engineer.
Not a chemist. Not a doctor. [pause] A mechanical engineer with a gift for selling ideas.
His name was Thomas Midgley Junior.
Remember that name. History will hang it next to two of the worst mistakes ever made.
